ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Synthesis and Exploration: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the quadratic function $y=x^2+bx+c$ passes through point $A\left(0, -\frac{7}{4}\right)$ and point $B\left(1, \frac{1}{4}\right)$. Point $P$ is an arbitrary point on the graph of this function, with the x-coordinate $m$. A line segment $PQ$ is drawn parallel to the x-axis from point $P$, and the x-coordinate of point $Q$ is $-2m+1$. It is known that point $P$ and point $Q$ do not coincide, and the length of segment $PQ$ decreases as $m$ increases. What is the range of values for $m$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: $PQ=\left|-3m+1\right|$, \\
when $-3m+1>0$, $PQ=-3m+1$, the length of $PQ$ decreases as $m$ increases, \\
when $-3m+1<0$, $PQ=3m-1$, the length of $PQ$ increases as $m$ increases, \\
$\therefore$ $-3m+1>0$ satisfies the condition, \\
solving gives $\boxed{m<\frac{1}{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the accompanying figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, the horizontal axis is the x-axis, the vertical axis is the y-axis, and a parabola opening upward is drawn. Point A is marked near the y-axis and is below the x-axis; there is also a similar spare figure on the right. The image does not give additional numerical values, and is mainly consistent with the image of the quadratic function described in the problem statement. Reasoning: Since the function y=x^2+bx+c passes through A(0,-7/4), substituting x=0 gives c=-7/4. It also passes through B(1,1/4), substituting gives 1+b+c=1/4, so 1+b-7/4=1/4, solving gives b=1. Therefore the coordinates of P are (m, m^2+m-7/4). Because PQ is parallel to the x-axis, and the x-coordinate of Q is -2m+1, the length of PQ is equal to the absolute value of the difference between the x-coordinates of the two points: PQ=|(-2m+1)-m|=|1-3m|. P and Q do not coincide, so 1-3m≠0, that is, m≠1/3. Discuss by cases: when m<1/3, 1-3m>0, PQ=1-3m, and it decreases as m increases; when m>1/3, 1-3m<0, PQ=3m-1, and it increases as m increases. Therefore the range satisfying "the length of PQ decreases as m increases" is m<1/3.
